# Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta (Iti 15 (It 1.15 PTS It 8))

**ID:** Iti 15 (It 1.15 PTS It 8)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Fetter of Craving
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti15
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta* (Iti 15) is the fifteenth discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, situated in the *Ekakanipāta* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta delivers a succinct teaching declaring that beings bound by the fetter of craving (*taṇhāsaṁyojana*) wander and transmigrate through the round of rebirth (*saṁsāra*) for an exceedingly long time [SuttaCentral]. Together with its immediately preceding companion discourse, the *Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta* (Iti 14), it highlights craving and ignorance (*avijjā*) as the fundamental twin obstacles in human existence, keeping beings bound such that they cannot transcend the wandering from existence to existence (*itthabhāvaññathābhāva*) [Pande 1974; Webster 2005].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include a full Chinese parallel in the *Itivuttaka* translation T 765.2 (*Jié* 結), as well as passage-level parallels in the *Taṇhuppāda Sutta* (AN 4.9 and Iti 105), the *Dvayatānupassanā Sutta* (Snp 3.12), the Sanskrit *Ekottarikāgama* fragment SF 199, and the *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493) [SuttaCentral]. Machine-assisted text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus confirms close structural and textual alignment: its opening prose framing (§0.1–2.4) closely matches Iti 14, while its concluding verse segment (§3.1–4.4) is shared nearly verbatim with Snp 3.12 (§28.1–29.4), an agreement affirmed by both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also aligns this verse portion with canonical exegetical works such as the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23) and *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), as well as commentary collections (*Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*), alongside cross-language verse alignments in the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* [DharmaNexus].
